Export one outcome for MetaStan

Source: R/export_metastan.R
as_MetaStan.Rd

Builds MetaStan's arm-based input: one row per study with the number of arms nd and numbered arm columns, arm 1 being the control. Multi-arm studies (several rows sharing a control arm, see prepare_arm_data()) get one column set per arm.

Usage

as_MetaStan(
  data,
  outcome = NULL,
  ...,
  timepoint = NULL,
  measure = NULL,
  estimate_means = c("none", "wan", "qe"),
  design_effect = c("apply", "ignore"),
  output = c("metastan", "wide")
)

Arguments

data

An ma_data object or outcome data frame.

outcome

Outcome identifier(s), matched against outcome_id and then outcome_name. NULL keeps every outcome.

...

Unused; must be empty.

timepoint

Time point(s) to keep. NULL keeps every time point.

measure

Effect measure for every outcome. NULL uses each outcome's measure column.

estimate_means

For "MD" and "SMD": "none" (default) keeps studies as reported, so studies reporting only medians are flagged as incomplete; "wan" or "qe" first estimates missing means and SDs from medians, quartiles and ranges with convert_median_to_mean().

design_effect

"apply" (default) or "ignore"; see compute_effect_size().

output

"metastan" (default) returns the result of MetaStan::create_MetaStan_dat(), ready for MetaStan::meta_stan(); "wide" returns the one-row-per-study data frame it is built from.

Value

For "metastan", MetaStan's list (data_long, data_wide); for "wide", a data frame. Both carry the MetaStan likelihood in attr(x, "likelihood").

Details

measureMetaStan likelihoodArm columns
"OR", "RR""binomial"r1, n1, ... (events, sample size)
"MD""normal"M1, SE1, ... (mean, standard error)
"IRR""poisson"count1, exposure1, ...

Arm sizes, events and person-time are divided by the design effect (see compute_design_effect()); counts are then rounded, as the binomial and Poisson likelihoods need whole numbers. The reported sample sizes are kept as n_reported1, n_reported2, ... for forest plots.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
metastan_dat <- as_MetaStan(dat, outcome = "pain_24h", measure = "MD")
MetaStan::meta_stan(metastan_dat, likelihood = attr(metastan_dat, "likelihood"),
                    theta_prior = c(0, 1), tau_prior = 0.5)
} # }
